lines.speaker: DAUGHTER
lines.text: Mum… the next one’s in ten minutes, we can…

lines.speaker: HER
lines.text: Not waiting ten minutes, love.

lines.speaker: DAUGHTER
lines.text: When did that happen?

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: I’m 71 and I take the stairs faster than women half my age. Six weeks ago, I couldn’t.

lines.scene: HOOK B: THE LIFT QUEUE (up, with the shopping)
lines.speaker: DAUGHTER
lines.text: Mum, the lift’s just there.

lines.scene: HOOK B: THE LIFT QUEUE (up, with the shopping)
lines.speaker: HER
lines.text: So are the stairs.

lines.scene: HOOK B: THE LIFT QUEUE (up, with the shopping)
lines.speaker: DAUGHTER
lines.text: When did that happen?

lines.scene: HOOK B: THE LIFT QUEUE (up, with the shopping)
lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: I’m 71 and I take the stairs faster than women half my age. Six weeks ago, I couldn’t.

lines.speaker: TANNOY
lines.text: ...the escalator is out of service. Please use the stairs.

lines.speaker: COMMUTER
lines.text: You’re joking.

lines.speaker: HER
lines.text: It’s only stairs, love.

lines.speaker: DAUGHTER
lines.text: When did that happen?

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: I’m 71 and I take the stairs faster than women half my age. Six weeks ago, I couldn’t.

lines.speaker: DAUGHTER
lines.text: Mum, wait, I’ll give you a…

lines.speaker: DAUGHTER
lines.text: ...When did that happen?

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: I’m 71. Six weeks ago I couldn’t get up off my own floor.

lines.speaker: HER
lines.text: Just leave it by the stairs, love. I’ll get it later.

lines.speaker: HUSBAND
lines.text: I’ll bring it up.

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: Six weeks ago, I was going down my stairs backwards. One step at a time.

lines.speaker: HUSBAND
lines.text: Sleep alright?

lines.speaker: HER
lines.text: Fine, love.

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: If I’m being honest, some days I wasn’t going down them at all. I’d just stay upstairs.

lines.scene: SCENE 3: TRIED EVERYTHING + THE SUNDAY PLANT
lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: The full knee brace I bought slipped down my leg. By evening, it was around my ankle. I tried everything. Physiotherapy. Painkillers. Cortisone injections. Every brace and sleeve on the market.

lines.scene: SCENE 3: TRIED EVERYTHING + THE SUNDAY PLANT
lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: Nothing worked. Nothing lasted. Nothing gave me my life back.

lines.scene: SCENE 3: TRIED EVERYTHING + THE SUNDAY PLANT
lines.speaker: HUSBAND
lines.text: That drawer won’t shut soon.

lines.scene: SCENE 3: TRIED EVERYTHING + THE SUNDAY PLANT
lines.speaker: HER
lines.text: It shuts.

lines.scene: SCENE 3: TRIED EVERYTHING + THE SUNDAY PLANT
lines.speaker: SISTER
lines.text: Sunday… shall we just do the garden centre? It’s all one level.

lines.scene: SCENE 3: TRIED EVERYTHING + THE SUNDAY PLANT
lines.speaker: HER
lines.text: Course, love. Easier.

lines.scene: SCENE 3: TRIED EVERYTHING + THE SUNDAY PLANT
lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: My sister’s knees are worse than mine. We planned our Sundays around one level.

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: Then my granddaughter got married in June. My cousin Barbara was there. She’s 74. And she was on the dance floor all night.

lines.speaker: HER
lines.text: Her knees were worse than mine. Both of them. Bone on bone.

lines.speaker: HUSBAND
lines.text: Whose?

lines.speaker: HER
lines.text: Barbara’s.

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: I always assumed hers weren’t as bad as mine. I always assumed mine were past the point of fixing.

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: Barbara came to stay the week after. She watched me work through my morning routine.

lines.speaker: BARBARA
lines.text: Can I show you something?

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: A small black strap. Just below her kneecap.

lines.speaker: BARBARA
lines.text: They come in twos. I never used the spare.

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: It looked absurd. Too small.

lines.speaker: HER
lines.text: Barbara. This can’t possibly work on knees like mine.

lines.speaker: BARBARA
lines.text: Just put it on and walk down the stairs.

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: The first step, I didn’t have to hold the banister.

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: Not the second. Not the third.

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: All the way down. Both feet. Forwards.

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: First step. Pain gone. Like a switch.

lines.speaker: BARBARA
lines.text: Everything you’ve tried was designed to make you comfortable while your knee got worse. This one fixes why it hurts.

lines.speaker: BARBARA
lines.text: There’s one spot below the kneecap where every step lands. Every brace, every injection, every pill you’ve ever taken treated the whole knee. Not that spot.

lines.speaker: BARBARA
lines.text: That’s why nothing worked. The pain is pressure. Nothing more.

lines.speaker: BARBARA
lines.text: This sits on that spot and lifts the weight off.

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: Over 200,000 people wear one now. Sports doctors recommend it. Not the pharma companies. Sports doctors.

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: Barbara’s husband wears one. He’s 76. He plays golf twice a week. Her niece wears one for tennis. She’s 22.

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: I’ve worn mine every day for six weeks. Under my clothes. Nobody knows it’s there. No pills. No gel. No brace around my ankle by lunchtime.

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: Yesterday I walked into town. Two miles there. Two miles back. I outwalked three women half my age.

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: I stood in line for ten minutes without shifting my weight.

lines.speaker: CASHIER
lines.text: You alright carrying those, love?

lines.speaker: HER
lines.text: I am, actually.

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: I carried two bags home. Nobody helped me.

lines.speaker: HUSBAND
lines.text: You were gone a long time.

lines.speaker: HER
lines.text: I know.

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: That was six weeks of wearing the strap. Nothing else.

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: I’m not the one everyone waits for anymore.

lines.speaker: FRIEND 1
lines.text: Right. What’s changed? And don’t say a haircut.

lines.speaker: HER
lines.text: Three weeks ago I couldn’t have crossed this room like that.

lines.speaker: FRIEND 2
lines.text: So what is it?

lines.speaker: HER
lines.text: It’s a strap.

lines.speaker: FRIEND 1
lines.text: That little thing?

lines.speaker: HER
lines.text: That’s what I said.

lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: So I’m just going to say it here. It’s called Stryde. Patellar Force Redirection. It’s been designed for three years with orthopaedic surgeons. It’s the real thing. Not the cheap knockoffs they sell on Amazon and fake Shopify sites.

lines.scene: SCENE 13: THE OFFER, PLANTED IN THE STORY
lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: The link’s below. Two straps for the price of one right now. 60 days to send them back if they don’t work.

lines.scene: SCENE 13: THE OFFER, PLANTED IN THE STORY
lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: Eleven years of knee pain. Gone the first step I took with it on.

lines.scene: SCENE 13: THE OFFER, PLANTED IN THE STORY
lines.speaker: VO
lines.text: I bought a second pair for my sister the same week. She’s coming Sunday.

lines.scene: SCENE 13: THE OFFER, PLANTED IN THE STORY

lines.scene: SCENE 13: THE OFFER, PLANTED IN THE STORY
